title: Geo-locking controls for Hosted API with TTL-driven retention and signed compliance ledger
creator: Lena Chen
description: Deliver a first-class Hosted API feature that lets tenants declare and enforce geographic residency policies (geo-locking) with per-tenant defaulting and request-level overrides, plus TTL-driven retention enforcement and a signed, downloadable compliance ledger for audits. The scope spans API surface additions, Console UX, runtime routing policy integration, retention enforcement in the ingestion pipeline, and an evidence export format for legal/compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Console exposes a per-tenant geo-locking control with clear precedence and a toggle for 'soft-fallback' behavior
Hosted API supports a Residency-Manifest header and tenant default manifest; manifests accepted/rejected with clear validation errors
Requests routed according to residency manifest with metrics showing region hits and any fallback events
Retention TTLs applied at ingest; data older than tenant-specified TTL is deleted automatically and deletion events are recorded
Compliance ledger export (signed ZIP) bundles manifest snapshots, routing logs, deletion proofs (hashes & timestamps), and a human-readable audit summary
Evidence exports are verifiable (signature + log hashes) and downloadable via Console and API without exposing sensitive payloads
implementation_notes: API: add Residency-Manifest JSON schema; provide SDK helpers and server-side validation in control plane
Console: design a compact flow for setting tenant defaults and creating per-endpoint overrides; include soft-fallback explanation copy
Runtime: extend routing policy engine to evaluate residency manifests and choose region variant; emit telemetry for each decision
Ingest: retention enforcement job will be implemented as a ledger-driven GC that emits signed deletion receipts (hash + timestamp)
Evidence export: generate a signed ZIP containing manifest versions, routing trace subset (redacted request ids), deletion receipts, and a checksum index
Backward compatibility: when no residency manifest exists, current routing behavior retained; migration tool to backfill tenant default manifests from account metadata
Observability: add per-tenant metrics (region_hit_count, fallback_count, retention_deletion_count) and an internal dashboard for compliance review
open_questions: Should soft-fallback be opt-in per tenant or default-off for all new tenants?
What retention-granularity do legal teams require (per-tenant, per-route, per-request)?
Do we need HSM-signing for ledger exports or is platform key signing sufficient for initial rollout?
What retention grace-periods or legal holds workflows must we accommodate in the first iteration?
